tools.name: score_buying_signal_evidence
tools.description: Deterministically score caller-supplied business-account fit and buying-signal evidence. Returns a review-only scorecard, evidence gaps, and unsupported-claim flags. The tool does not fetch sources, access Intakra workspaces, store input, spend money, draft outreach, or send anything.

tools.name: prepare_why_now_review
tools.description: Turn caller-supplied fit criteria and business signals into reviewable why-now and fit guidance. Every fact remains labeled caller-supplied and unverified. The tool does not research, infer budget or buyer intent as fact, draft outreach, access private data, persist input, or take action.

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: Use for 'here is my account list' or 'which companies am I tracking?'. List accounts in your connected Intakra workspace, or match supplied domains against that list. Returns missing domains, recorded check dates and pagination. This reads saved records and does not add accounts or run a new check.

tools.name: prioritize_accounts
tools.description: Use for 'who should I target from my account list?' or 'are these companies showing buying signals?'. Rank your tracked accounts by their saved open opportunities relevant to your offering (and by Intakra's account score for fit, timing and reach, 0 to 100, when it is on for your workspace), with da

tools.name: get_account_changes
tools.description: Use for 'anything happening on my account list?' or 'what changed at these companies this week?'. Return newly recorded findings for your tracked accounts since a chosen date, with the public event date, the date Intakra recorded it and source links. Defaults to the last seven days. Optional domains

tools.name: list_opportunities
tools.description: List the current leads: companies on your list that started something you could help with. Each one has what we found (with dates and links), what it usually means for someone selling what you sell, and a rough time frame. Use filter "closing_soon" for the ones that usually wind down within 30 days.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Read saved context for one company on your tracked list: up to 12 recent findings from public sources (with dates and available links), and current open leads with dated proof. Pass a domain (acme.com), a company name, or an account id. This does not run a new check.

tools.name: get_project_updates
tools.description: Read this workspace's watch status and the latest 20 material changes, with before/after claims and dated sources. Saved evidence only; no new research or notification.

tools.name: add_accounts
tools.description: Add companies to your list by website domain (for example ["acme.com", "globex.com"]). We start checking their public records on the next daily pass. Domains already on your list are skipped, and your plan's account limit applies.

tools.name: set_offering
tools.description: Tell Intakra what you sell, in a sentence or two (for example "Payroll software for restaurant groups with 5 to 50 locations"). We use it to decide which findings are worth your time. It replaces the current description.

tools.name: get_daily_brief
tools.description: Use for 'what should I look at today?' or 'who is worth a call?'. Returns the accounts in today's note: what we found (dated, with links), what it usually means for what you sell, who to reach and why, and roughly how much time there is. If no note went out yet today, returns what the next one would

tools.name: get_best_contact
tools.description: The person who most likely owns the project behind one lead, and why: name, role, LinkedIn, and a verified work email when we have one (never for EU, EEA or UK companies). Sometimes only a LinkedIn search for the right title. Who and why only: Intakra never writes or sends messages.

tools.name: list_suggestions
tools.description: Accounts Intakra suggested for your list (from public filings, news, and lookalikes of your customers), with the reason for each. Suggestions do not count toward your plan until you approve them in Intakra.

tools.name: request_accounts
tools.description: Ask Intakra to find companies that fit, from a short description, an industry, a size range, a country, or up to 5 of your customers' domains. findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_accounts" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: score_buying_signal_evidence, get_project_updates, get_best_contact · Private data: prepare_why_now_review, list_accounts, prioritize_accounts, get_account_changes, add_accounts, get_daily_brief, get_best_contact · Public sink: score_buying_signal_evidence, get_best_contact · Destructive: list_accounts, prioritize_accounts, get_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: score_buying_signal_evidence, get_project_updates, get_best_contact · Private data: prepare_why_now_review, list_accounts, prioritize_accounts, get_account_changes, add_accounts, get_daily_brief, get_best_contact · Public sink: score_buying_signal_evidence, get_best_contact · Destructive: list_accounts, prioritize_accounts, get_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
